issue.title: Restore the CI usage target for the expanded browser suite
issue.description:
The expanded browser suite no longer meets the user's requested 20% Actions usage reduction. The current successful PR #36 Web run 37268219679 and main Pages run 37268626778 use 326 runner seconds/eight rounded minutes, versus 307 seconds/eight minutes in the retained baseline pair 37131752983/37131749773. Raw usage increased 6.19%; rounded savings are zero. Projected artifact storage is 63.25% lower.

The historical 168-case sample achieved a 25% quota reduction; it is not current-suite acceptance. The current suite has 258 configured cases, 249 first-attempt passes, nine CDP-only skips, 116 units and subpath verification.

Acceptance:

- [ ] Identify measured bottlenecks and implement independently reviewed changes.
- [ ] A current equivalent successful PR/main pair reaches at least 20% lower rounded minutes and artifact byte-hours, with raw runner time improved.
- [ ] Preserve browser/lifecycle/normal-motion coverage, independent exact expectations, integrity, main-only exact-artifact publishing and bounded diagnostics. Do not skip assertions, mask retries or multiply jobs at higher quota cost.

An independent read-only investigation finds browser work dominates: 246 seconds of the 301-second Web job; 249 cases total 939.247 concurrent test-seconds. Controls total 182.2 seconds, app cases 177.06 and updates 130. The largest menu sweep totals 94.2 seconds. Next step: bounded Linux operation timing to choose an evidence-backed improvement. Full option rendering, protocol observation overhead and retry synchronization are hypotheses, not established optimizations.

Current reviewed runtime head: 9c7965a; merged main: 67be609. [Measurement and investigation](<https://github.com/Tien-Lam/ChronoShift/tree/main/docs/qa/ci-lifecycle-2026-10-05>). Workload expansion and timing variability must remain explicit; these samples do not claim monthly account totals.

5 October progress: draft PR #37 preserves all 258 configured scenarios and adds bounded sanitized timing metadata. Instrumented four-worker control 37269816926 passed 249 browser cases plus nine capability skips, with no retries or dropped attempts; its job took 356 seconds, browser step 291 seconds. This diagnostic run has no corresponding main publication and is not a new paired acceptance sample. Local scalar batching (22.5s versus 22.8s) showed no useful gain and was excluded, with the prototype/review retained. Six-worker same-job experiment 37270362546 is running at head 77fbf61; no added runner/job, coverage or motion changes. Both independent reviewers found no isolation blocker to the experiment; adoption and efficiency verdicts remain pending. Final uninstrumented full gate and matching publication pair are required. Evidence: docs/qa/ci-efficiency-2026-10-05/.

Current experiment result: six-worker CI 37270362546 is rejected (419-second job versus the instrumented four-worker control's 356 seconds). It completed with 259 attempts across 258 unique scenarios: one failed iPhone rollback attempt followed by a passing retry, plus nine capability skips. Four workers are restored. The green workflow conclusion was initially misreported as retry-free; original evidence and a separate correction are retained. Draft PR #37 now evaluates optional timing, successful-reuse publishing in one job with the full fallback retained, and bounded timezone virtualization. No efficiency target or final adoption is claimed. A mobile test precondition is being strengthened with a real field click and explicit automatic-open proof; actual frozen-origin identity is required because the WebKit fixture overrides config.baseURL.

Superseding progress: virtualization is fully removed; every web source file matches baseline main 7059. Its complete gate passed without retries but took 431s, and a bounded keyboard/scroll review blocker remained. Two-worker same-job run 37273144333 also passed 258 cases/116 units/subpath without retries but took 464s, so that setting is rejected. Actual resource metadata reports four CPUs and no own-cgroup throttling/OOM; it does not prove an optimal worker setting. Current candidate 52e8d9c restores four workers and measures standard ubuntu-24.04-arm using the identical cryptographically verified official multi-platform browser image. Full case identities, profiles, normal motion, expectations, integrity and retention stay unchanged. Trusted main static publishing uses a consolidated Ubuntu Slim job; complete fallback remains. Independent exact-source reviews, ARM full gate, actual fast/manual-fallback publishing and final paired metrics remain required. No quota target completion claim.
